setup: Start with the bench at a slight decline
Hook your feet under the pads
Arms across your chest or hands by your head
execution: Curl your chin and chest up first
Keep curling until your torso is upright
Breathe out on the way up
faults: Don't yank yourself up with your arms
Don't jerk up with a flat, arched back
Don't drop back onto the pad

notes: The hip muscles do much of the work in a full sit-up. Curling the chest up first keeps more of it on the abs.
Lying head-down makes some people light-headed. Sit up slowly between sets and stop if you feel dizzy.
Coaching sources differ on how much full sit-up volume is wise. Keep it moderate and build up gradually.
To add load, hold a plate on your chest and log it as added weight. Sit up fully before you unhook your feet.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at bench height. Decline bench with the head end low on the left and the foot rollers high on the right, at a shallow angle (about 20-30°).

keyPositions.label: Down
keyPositions.describe: Lying back on the decline bench, feet hooked under the rollers, knees bent. Back flat on the pad, arms crossed on the chest.

keyPositions.label: Curling
keyPositions.describe: Chin, chest and upper back curled up off the pad; lower back still touching. The curl leads before the hips start to bend.

keyPositions.label: Up
keyPositions.describe: Torso lifted off the pad to roughly upright, back still gently rounded, arms crossed on the chest. Feet still hooked.

ikHints: Pelvis stays on the seat end of the bench
emphasise: The chest curls up first, then the hips bend
Slow, rounded lowering back to the pad
doNotShow: Arms swinging to throw the body up

uncertain.note: ExRx files this exercise under the hip flexors (iliopsoas target) with the abs as stabilisers unless the waist curls. The abs are listed first because the cues ask for the curl; hip_flexors is a primary too (vocabulary word added 23 Oct 2026, expansion research Q1). How the work splits between them depends on how much the waist curls.
A decline or ab bench has no station value. specific_machine is the nearest; the domain doesn't check it.
Spine and hips both move, so this could be called compound. Kept as isolation to match the other ab-curl and leg-raise entries.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data.
